title: Broadway Is My Beat
paragraphs: A moody New York police drama following Detective Danny Clover through homicide cases and the people of the Broadway precinct, with the city itself serving as a major part of the atmosphere.

CBS police/crime drama following homicide detective Danny Clover through the Broadway/Times Square district. Frozen GRH snapshot contains 153 dated episodes from March 6, 1949 through August 22, 1953, not the full run through August 1, 1954.

GRH documents the program through New York Anthony Ross era (February 27, 1949 to May 29, 1949) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]], Hollywood summer era (July 7, 1949 to August 25, 1949) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]], and Hollywood main run (November 5, 1949 to August 1, 1954) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are [[person|larry-thor|Larry Thor]] (performer on 145 recordings), Charles Calvert (performer on 144 recordings), Elliott Lewis (director on 128 recordings, producer on 127 recordings, performer on 7 recordings, and transcriber on 1 recording), Alexander Courage (composer on 132 recordings, conductor on 92 recordings, arranger on 1 recording, music on 1 recording, and performer on 1 recording), Jack Kruschen (performer on 117 recordings), David Friedkin (writer on 90 recordings and performer on 2 recordings), and Morton Fine (writer on 90 recordings).

The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] (broadcast on network), [[org|org.cd82fd99edb39caa|Armed Forces Radio and Television Service]] (rebroadcast by), and [[org|org.4798d1172deaae2c|Armed Forces Radio Service]] (rebroadcast by).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include murder and homicide, juvenile crime and vulnerable youth, Manhattan and New York street life, Broadway, theater and nightlife, robbery and theft, and suicide and staged suicide.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Broadway and Times Square as dramatic environment, Hollywood production of a New York police drama, Postwar urban police drama, and CBS utility and summer-replacement scheduling.
